core_claim.P: When CrossAdapter.updatePriceFeeds is called with inverse direction parameters (QUOTE, BASE), where the contract supports both forward and inverse directions for price queries like getQuote
core_claim.I: updatePriceFeeds should handle the inverse direction the same way getQuote does, checking direction and calling the correct oracles in the correct order
core_claim.V: updatePriceFeeds lacks the direction check, so the oracles are queried about token pairs they don't know, return wrong fees (likely 0), and the transaction reverts because the total fee doesn't match what was sent

distinct_impacts.description: Any call to updatePriceFeeds with inverse parameters reverts
distinct_impacts.evidence_quote: Any call to updatePriceFeeds with inverse parameters will revert

distinct_impacts.description: Prices become stale because markets needing inverse direction pricing cannot update prices
distinct_impacts.evidence_quote: If a market needs inverse direction pricing, it can't update prices

distinct_impacts.description: Users trade at worse rates than they should due to stale prices
distinct_impacts.evidence_quote: Stale prices mean users trade at worse rates than they should

distinct_impacts.description: Inconsistent behavior between getQuote (works both ways) and updatePriceFeeds (only one way)
distinct_impacts.evidence_quote: getQuote works both ways, but updatePriceFeeds only works one way

distinct_impacts.description: Oracles are asked about token pairs they don't know and return wrong fees (likely 0), causing the fee mismatch revert
distinct_impacts.evidence_quote: The oracles return wrong fees (likely 0) because they're being asked about token pairs they don't know about. Then the transaction reverts because the total fee doesn't match what was sent.
